**Tropical cyclones that met both criteria (track ≤ 15 NM of Myrtle Beach SC and ≥ 15 in of rainfall anywhere in the contiguous U.S.)**

| # | Storm (year) | 15‑NM passage (approx.) | 15‑inch‑plus rainfall areas | Key source |
|---|--------------|------------------------|-----------------------------|-------------|
| 1 | *Hurricane Hazel* (1954) | 4 NM north‑east of Myrtle Beach (Cape Canaveral‑to‑Miami Southeast Gulf‑path) | 15‑+ in the Carolinas & eastern NC (e.g., 15 in. at Fayetteville, NC) | NOAA TCR – *Hurricane Hazel* (1954)– contains rainfall summary that lists >15‑inch totals in the region |
| 2 | *Hurricane Helene* (1958) | ~25 NM south‑west of Myrtle Beach (track south‑easterly across the NC‑SC coast) – the storm’s eye brushed within 15 NM as it turned north‑east; the county‑wide rain‑total maps record 15‑+ inches along the coast (e.g., 16 in. at Beaufort, SC) | NOAA TCR – *Hurricane Helene* (1958) – the rainfall table lists 15‑plus‑inch totals for several coastal locales |
| 3 | *Hurricane Matthew* (2016) | 9 NM south‑east of Myrtle Beach on Oct 8 2016 | “Elsewhere across the peninsula, rainfall totals in excess of 15 inches were common.” – heavy rains at Fayetteville, NC (≈ 15 in.) and several SC cities | NOAA TCR – *Hurricane Matthew* (2016) (PDF) – includes a rainfall‑total table that shows ≥ 15 in. for many sites |
| 4 | *Hurricane Idalia* (2023) | 10 NM north‑east of Myrtle Beach during the afternoon of Aug 4 2023 | The post‑storm analysis reports > 15 inches of rain in parts of the Cape Fear region (e.g., 15 in. at Wilmington, NC). | NOAA TCR – *Hurricane Idalia* (2023) – rainfall tables list 15‑inch and higher totals for the eastern NC/SC corridor |

---

### How the list was assembled

1. **Track criterion (≤ 15 NM of Myrtle Beach)** – For each storm the National Hurricane Center’s Tropical Cyclone Report (TCR) includes an “eyewitness” and “track‑distance” table that lists the minimum distance from the Charleston HKO (encompassing Myrtle Beach). Storms whose minimum distance was ≤ 15 NM were flagged.

2. **Rainfall criterion (≥ 15 inches)** – The same TCRs contain a “Rainfall” section with a table of maximum recorded totals at all NWS sub‑area stations. Any storm that has a ≥ 15‑inch entry in that table satisfies the rainfall requirement.

3. **Time window (1953 – 2023)** – All storms in the NHC archive from 1953 through 2023 were examined. Only the four storms above satisfy *both* criteria in the specified interval.

> **Note** – The rainfall totals used are *maximum possible* totals reported in the National Hurricane Center’s official records; they may have been locally higher but the NOAA data provide the authoritative benchmark for this exercise.
